system.summary: Book code on Entick's New Spelling Dictionary (London 1776 setting): page, column a/b and entry number down the column, with written endings; persons from the dictionary's list of Christian names (five columns a-e).
system.notes: Groups written page, column letter, roman line number (once arabic), separated by commas; endings after a dash. Entry count skips running heads, section headings and run-over lines.

prior_solution.where: The received copies of letters 2 (22 April 1779), 3 (27 April 1779) and 4 (21 May 1779) carry an old decipherment interlined above the code groups, in two layers (skeleton letters in a darker hand; fuller words, often queried, in a fainter hand; writers not identified; one copy annotated 'The decyphering in this is for the most part conjectural'): Lee Family Papers, University of Virginia, microfilm ed. Hoffman and Molyneaux (1966), roll 6, Internet Archive per_lee-family-papers_the-lee-family-papers_1742-1795_6, images n73-n75, n109-n111, n203-n211. Scored against this reading after it was frozen (received/): 63 of 72 comparable groups agree; the nine differences are the interliner's guesses (e.g. 'Court (King?)' for minister at 243a17, 'sail' for return). Burnett's typed partial key (Library of Congress copy, filmed on roll 1, images n188-n203) gives values for 39 of the 119 distinct groups. No received copy or decipherment of letters 1, 5 and 6 found. No printed reading found: not in Burnett's Letters of Members III-IV, Ballagh, Smith's Letters of Delegates 12-13, Life of Arthur Lee (1829), Wharton, Sparks, Tomokiyo or Hays's 1899 calendar; Potts (1981) searched inside only, Weber (1979) index only.

solution.what: Paged all 227 images of PCC item 102 vol. 3 (catalog 502968528) at contact-sheet size, then 1000 px; image 0041 showed bare dictionary-code groups in a letter to R. H. Lee. Six letters, 166 groups, inventoried.
One transcription of the six letters with all 166 groups from the 1610-px images; 24 groups marked doubtful.

Tomokiyo's Cryptiana (system and about a dozen groups), Burnett 1917 and Letters of Members III-IV (other direction, 1782 edition), Ballagh, Life of Arthur Lee, Wharton, Sparks, Papers of John Adams 8: no reading of these letters.

Compared Entick editions 1766, 1772, 1773, 1776, 1781 against Tomokiyo's anchor groups; 1776 London setting chosen, entry-count rule fixed on loan 229a37 and I 196a28. Test plan frozen (sha256) before decoding.
All 166 groups looked up by eye on the 1776 page images; readings graded firm, guess or unread; four cut-off page numbers supplied from sense.

Frozen test on 30 random groups: real 27/30 fit, controls page+1 0/22, page-1 1/22, page+7 0/23, page-7 0/28, 1772 edition 1/25. Weak: the same agent extracted and judged, contexts showed decoded neighbours, controls are random words.

Independent check by a second AI agent, blind to the reading: rule-chosen sample of 54 groups (24 doubtful + 30 by rule), edition and rule decided from Tomokiyo's groups alone, table frozen before opening the reader's files. Same word 43 of 54; 29 of 30 in the rule sample. Settled the 1776 printing against 1773 (court 108a9); found the reader's p. 166 edition claim wrong; read letter-book p. 39 (no code).

Hays's calendar of the Lee correspondence at the American Philosophical Society (Proceedings of the APS 38, 1899): Arthur Lee to R. H. Lee entries run 1768-1774 only; none of the six dates; no mention of cipher. Society's digital library: 404 then 403, not searched.

Received copies of letters 2-4 (Lee Family Papers microfilm roll 6) read group by group after freezing the key and reading (sha256, received/FREEZE_received.txt) and writing the scoring rule; one scoring run over 95 groups: 45 same word, 18 other form or abbreviation, 9 different word (interliner's guesses or identifications), 23 absent or too short; 63 of 72 comparable groups agree. Then six groups regraded on the groups as the received copies write them (distress, exertions, politicians, contempt, second Benjamin firm; chaplain/character doubtful), and letter 4 dated 21 May 1779.

Lee Family Papers microfilm: 1966 guide and Burnett's typed partial key on roll 1 (key gives values for 39 of our 119 distinct groups; 33 same word, 3 other form, 3 different); received copies of letters 1, 5, 6 looked for on rolls 5-6 by contact sheet (roll 5 n1190-n1244; roll 6 n13-n66, n501-n640, n851-n899, plus dates every fifty images n700-n1200) and not found; roll 7 and the undated section not paged.

Second search of the Lee Family Papers microfilm (roll 5 n1100-n1189; roll 6 every image n13-n1248; roll 7 sampled; roll 8 item) and of the three finding aids filmed on roll 1 (University of Virginia name index, American Philosophical Society calendar, Harvard calendar): no received copy of letters 1, 5 and 6; Virginia Historical Society and Library of Congress not checked. Found a received copy of a further letter, 21 August 1779 (roll 6 n474-n476), whose three groups read Governor, Archibald, Car-y (Cary, numeral doubtful); its letter-book entry (image 0095, dated 20 August) has the words struck out. An unsigned coded letter on roll 6 n227-n229 is R. H. Lee to Arthur Lee, 22-23 May 1779, already printed decoded (Burnett IV no. 295; Smith 12:513-515); 14 of 15 of its groups give the printed word in the 1776 setting.

Held-out test on 71 groups glossed at the time in Arthur Lee's letters of 27 and 31 August 1778 and 21 May 1779 (M247 item 83 vol. 1 images 258-259, 261; vol. 2 images 232-233, 237), none used to build the reading. Plan and pass mark (80% same word or other form; controls under 10%) written first; a second agent looked the groups up blind by the frozen rule and froze its table (gloss1778/FREEZE_lookup.txt) before the glosses were written. Result 54 of 71 (76%): below the mark, so the test as planned failed. Controls page +1, page -1, other column, 1781 printing 0 of 71 each; 1773 printing 44. Second look after scoring: three misses are our misreadings of the clerk's figure 4 (the rule gives Sorry, Affair, Minister at the corrected places), four are look-ups without a 1776 image or OCR text, four look like Lee's slips, one is the decipherer's wording (sinking/redeeming), four unexplained (Florida, 'a noble', two groups under 'Treaty of Alliance').

Looked for a second scan of the London 1776 Entick: Internet Archive (one copy only, the one already used), Google Books by ordinary viewing (no 1776 or 1777 copy; full views from 1780 on, paged differently), HathiTrust (stopped at the first 403 to a script), Eighteenth Century Collections Online (no signed-in tab). None found. Fetched 22 further pages of the same 1776 scan instead (pp. 22, 94, 96, 172, 201, 237, 253, 255, 256, 262, 268, 289, 290, 295, 299, 300, 325, 338, 339, 356, 359, 364).

Second look, after the first gloss test's score, at its 17 misses on 1600-pixel images of the letters and on the 1776 dictionary pages (score not changed): nine are misreadings of the figures by our transcriber (347, 40, 243 as before; also 253 read as 233, 165 as 163, 259 as 359, 43,a,XXIII as 63,a,XXVI, 364,b,XVIII as XXIII, probably 361,b,XXIX as XXX); two had no image and give the glossed word on the image (Conclude, 96b20); three are the decipherer's words where the rule's word fits the sentence (Sink 'sinking' the paper; No 'She has made no motion', glossed 'a noble'; Your 'to your worthy constituents', glossed 'you'); two are Lee one entry off (Stipulation for stipulate; Serviceable for service, which is right if the run-over line of Sergeant is counted); one unexplained (300,b,IX Quarryman for 'quarrel'). Lee's instructions of 3 June 1776 (item 83 vol. 1 images 27-28) prescribe a different method (page plus a letter for the word's place on the whole page) in an unnamed book.

Second gloss test (second attempt, after the first failed), plan written first (gloss1778/TEST_PLAN_gloss2.md): a helper who never saw the glosses transcribed the 71 groups from strips cut to hide the interlined words (frozen, gloss1778/FREEZE_transcribed2.txt), a second helper looked them up blind in the 1776 images with controls (frozen, gloss1778/FREEZE_lookup2.txt). Seed groups passed in both. Result 55 of 71 (77.5%): below the 80% mark, so the second test also failed. Controls: page +1 1 of 71 (a transcription slip, 242 for 243), page -1, other column and 1781 printing 0 of 71. Without the six anchor occurrences 52 of 65 (80%). Nine of the 16 misses are the new transcriber's misreadings of the figures.

Re-read the 11 doubtful and 4 unread groups on full-size letter-book images (about 2,700 px; images 0019, 0035, 0041, 0123) and in the 1776 dictionary: one moves to firm (63,a,XXXII Betray: the second I is on the image before the paper edge); the others are unchanged. Counts 151 firm, 11 doubtful, 4 unread.

Catalogues for received copies of letters 1, 5 and 6 (20 minutes): Virginia Museum of History and Culture lists Lee Family Papers Mss1 L51 f (1638-1867, 684 items) and Mss1 L51 b (1732-1892, 71 items), item lists not online to us; a web search of Library of Congress finding aids found no Arthur Lee or Richard Henry Lee papers collection (the Ethel Armes Collection of Lee Family Papers was not opened); Harvard's HOLLIS for Archival Discovery search pages failed in the browser, Arthur Lee papers known only through SNAC (1741-1882). Nothing for the three dates; nothing digitized. Upstream lead 1435 cites a New York Public Library item: Arthur Lee to Samuel Adams, 27 April 1779, with an enclosed list 'Cyphers A.L. to S.A.' (Samuel Adams papers, MssCol 20), digitized; it is a small numbered nomenclator of names and words (1 to 62), not the Entick code, and settles no group.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 162 tokens, 115 types, en-modern order 4: reading -2.219 per letter; random keys -2.238 (z 0.5); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -1.945 (mean -1.955, z -25.1); annealer on the real text -1.957. Verdict: underdetermined.

Double reading of every figure (plan frozen first, double_read/TEST_PLAN_double_read.md): two blind Opus readers, who had seen neither our transcription nor each other's, transcribed page, column and line of all 166 groups from overlapping strips of the 1610-px letter-book images, seeded with known groups from Lee's letters of 1778-79 (batch 1 was redone once after both readers misread the seed 81,b,XX as 84; the redo of reader B missed it again and is used with that stated). The readers agree with each other on 162 of 166 groups and with our transcription on 161 (A) and 159 (B); all three on 158. Rule: firm only if two independent readings agree on page, column and line and the entry fits. Our transcription was wrong on 1 group (455,d,XXVII, column written 'a?') and had the right figure only as its alternative on 1 more (63,a,XXXII): figure-reading error rate 1 of 166 (0.6%), 2 of 166 (1.2%) counting the alternative. Four groups stay unsettled: charges (82 or 12), exertions (blot; 152 only on the received copy), contempt (the copies differ, 100 and 101), Gerard or Thomas (blot). Counts 148 firm, 14 doubtful, 4 unread.

Third gloss test (third attempt after two misses), plan frozen first (gloss1778/TEST_PLAN_gloss3.md): Arthur Lee to Henry Laurens, Paris, 7 Dec 1778 (University of South Carolina, South Caroliniana Library, digital collection amerrevsc item 1888; upstream lead 1435), 19 groups glossed in a contemporary hand. Strips hiding the glosses were cut by a separate agent; two blind Opus readers transcribed them (the first pair rejected on a seed; of the redo pair one missed the same seed, used with that stated); disagreements were settled on the strips before any look-up; the look-up on the 1776 page images was frozen before the glosses were read. Result 10 of 19 (53%; 9 of 19 without one abbreviated gloss): far below the 80% mark, so the third test failed. Controls page +1, page -1 and other column 0 of 19. Second look after scoring: seven of the nine misses are misread figures in the hand of the sent letter (1 read as 5 three times, giving pages 570-579 that the dictionary does not have; 218, 384 and 283 misread; one column b read as a); six of the seven give the glossed word at the figures the glosses imply.

William Lee to Richard Henry Lee, Frankfurt, 15 Oct 1778 (Lee Family Papers roll 5, images n574-n575; 13 groups, 12 different; not added to the 166 groups or the counts), plan frozen first (william_lee_1778/frozen_2026-11-15/TEST_PLAN.md): two blind readers agree on 13 of 13 figures; blind column lists of the 1776 page images give a word for all 13 (william_lee_1778/groups.tsv). New word: 140 a XXVIII = eclat, where the typed notes on roll 1 have 110 a XXVIII 'criticism?' (110a28 in 1776 = Crinkle); the other 11 words were already written over the passage in those notes.

William Lee, 15 Oct 1778, against prior values (typed notes and Burnett's key on roll 1, and Deane) and controls: the rule gives the prior word in 9 of 11 (mark 9; 10 if Frankly + in counts as frank[lin]); page + 1, page - 1 and other column 0 of 11 each. Blind fit judge: rule word fits 12 of 12 blanks, control words 0 of 36.

William Lee, 15 Oct 1778: second blind look-up of the 12 columns from the 1776 page images by a fresh agent (plan hashed before it started; seed 80 a XVI = Cavalier found): 12 of 12 agree with the first look-up (william_lee_1778/frozen_2026-11-17/).

Ford, Letters of William Lee II (1891) 491-493 (Internet Archive letterswilliaml00leegoog; pp. 491-492 and 417-418 read on the page images, p. 493 in the text layer only): the 13 groups printed as figures, unread, the fifth as 110 a xxviii; three names footnoted from the sense (Benjamin Franklin, Deane, Williams nephew of Franklin).

Integration review for the write-up: the six readings read as sentences and graded (reading_review replaced the author's preliminary grades); escalation checklist reviewed (print ticked: Weber p. 53 and Potts are lending-only, recorded as a needs-physical-access gap); Transcription doubts listed in NOTES from decoding.tsv, the double reading and the received copies; a crop of letter 4 cut from the National Archives Catalog image 0041 for the page.

texts.label: Letter 1, [29 March 1779]
texts.summary: Lee tells his brother that La Luzerne is to replace Gérard as French minister, that the 'friend' (adjective doubtful) and his assistants are promoting Deane's [charges?], that French 'faith & friendship' (the first word is written Frenchified) count for nothing beside interest, and that the French nation begins to talk against the alliance. Lee's private opinions, not established facts.
texts.note: read_share: words of the Reading section without a doubtful mark (?) or hole, 284 of 293. Code groups: 38 firm, 6 doubtful, 0 unread of 44.

reading_review.by: integration review of 24 Nov 2026 (AI agent, for the maintainers); not a person
reading_review.note: Grade given by the reviewer, not by the author of the reading; it replaces the author's preliminary self-check of 14 Nov 2026. Read readings/l1.md as sentences: coherent English throughout (La Luzerne to replace Gerard; the friend and his assistants promoting Deane's charges; French faith and friendship worth nothing beside interest; the nation begins to talk against the alliance). Six doubtful words are bracketed with a query, two of them with both candidates; one hole is letters lost at the page edge. Grade A, scattered doubts, every sentence followable. Checked against decoding.tsv and the letter's transcription; not against the manuscript images in this review. A model's reading: no person has checked it.

texts.label: Letter 2, 22 April 1779
texts.summary: Lee reports that Gérard is suspected in Paris of dealings with Deane in merchandise and contracts, and gives his opinion that 'the Doctor', the French consul, Gérard, Deane, Chaumont and Beaumarchais are 'all interested together'; the French court is short of money for the war. Lee's charges, written privately.

texts.label: Letter 3, 27 April 1779
texts.summary: Since Gérard's recall, Lee writes, people in Paris talk of his 'connexion in jobs' with Deane and Beaumarchais; 'a certain person here' is an instrument of those the French court set over him; Congress should resolve that the attacks on the Lees were unjust.

texts.label: Letter 4, 21 May 1779
texts.summary: Spain has fifty ships of the line but has not declared; 'the Marquis your Brigadeer' is to return with 2,000 French men (the next word is doubtful), and Lee suspects the French 'wish for a footing'. 'Never will our affairs go well, while Benjamin is here'; whether to present his piece against 'the old Doctor' depends on 'the part taken by John Adams'. Whom 'he is the servant of this court' means is not in the code.

texts.label: Letter 5, 27 September 1779
texts.summary: Lee protests at an anonymous letter of abuse received by Congress against two commissioners, calls Gérard's conduct a 'wicked manoeuvre', warns of a man (name unread) who wants to be 'alternately governor & delegate' in Virginia, and gives plans for two of his brother's sons.
